title: A Patient-Derived Xenograft Model of Glioblastoma
protocol: Add 100–200 μL of Liberase stock solution to 15 mL of PBS.
Warm the Liberase-PBS solution to 37°C.
Warm an aliquot of 0.8% ammonium chloride solution to 37°C.
Warm NeuroCult Complete (NCC) media to 37°C.
Place the patient brain tumor specimen in a 100 mm cell culture dish.
Gently pipette 5 - 10 mL of PBS onto the sample to wash away RBCs and other fluids.
Discard the PBS without disturbing the specimen.
Mechanically dissociate the tumor sample into pieces <2 mm3 using surgical scissors and forceps.
Aliquot and snap freeze a small amount of tumor sample (~5%–10% or at least 3 mm3) at −80°C for downstream analyses.
Transfer the mechanically-dissociated tumor specimen into 15 mL pre-warmed PBS with Liberase.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 min in an incubator-shaker (30 rpm).
Filter the tissue lysate through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new tube to separate undigested tissue.
Centrifuge filtrate at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant carefully and resuspend pellet in 1 mL of PBS.
Add 4 - 12 mL of ammonium chloride solution proportional to the pellet size and RBC infiltration.
Incubate for 5 min.
After incubation, add an equivalent amount of PBS.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Decant supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 mL of pre-warmed NCC media.
Add 10 μL of the cell suspension to 10 μL of Trypan Blue.
Mix well and count cells using a hemocytometer, as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer the cell suspension to either a 100 mm or a 60 mm ultra-low-binding tissue culture dish.
If the total number of cells is less than 1 million, plate cells in a 60 mm CELLSTAR® Cell-Repellent tissue culture dish with 3 mL of total NCC media.
If the total number of cells exceeds 1 million, plate up to 2.5 million cells in a 100 mm CELLSTAR® Cell-Repellent tissue culture dish with 7–10 mL of total NCC media.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 48 h.
When the media changes color from red to orange or 72 h have passed after plating cells, add 2 - 4 mL of NCC media to the cell culture dish.
Change media completely when the media color turns slightly yellow.
Warm fresh NCC media to 37°C before starting media replacement.
Pipette cell culture to a sterile tube.
Rinse the culture dish with 5–10 mL of PBS and add it to the same tube.
Centrifuge for 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of warm NCC media.
Gently add the cell solution to the cell culture dish with additional media as recommended by the manufacturer.
Transfer cell culture to a sterile tube.
Rinse the culture dish with 5–10 mL of PBS and add it to the same tube.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of PBS.
Add 3–5 μL of Liberase stock solution (2.5 μg/μL) to the cell suspension.
Add 5–10 μL DNase I stock solution (2000 U/mL in PBS) to the cell suspension.
Incubate in a 37°C water bath for 5 minutes or less.
If tumorspheres are still visible after initial incubation, incubate for an additional 2–5 minutes.
Do not exceed 15 minutes of total incubation time to avoid significant cell death.
Pipette up and down gently using a micropipette to aid complete cell dissociation.
Add 5–10 mL of PBS to the cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 500–1,000 μL of PBS or in 1 mL of NCC media for replating.
For use in assays, filter the cell suspension into a 12 × 75 mm tube with a 35 μm cell strainer cap.
Determine cell number and viability using Trypan blue solution.
Adjust cell count as required for specific assays or replating.
Mix poly-L-ornithine and sterile water in a 1:3 ratio to coat the dish surface completely.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Remove poly-L-ornithine solution from the dish.
Wash the culture dish with 2–5 mL of sterile water.
Add PBS containing 4 μg/mL laminin to coat the surface completely.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for up to 12 hours as needed.
Resuspend desired cell solution in warm NCC media, equaling 5%–10% of the dish's working volume.
Remove laminin solution and wash the culture dish immediately before plating cells with sterile PBS.
Add the cell solution drop-wise to the coated dish.
Place the dish gently into an incubator.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes to 1 hour.
Incubate tumorspheres for 5 min at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Gently rock the plate to check if tumorspheres have adhered using a microscope.
If tumorspheres do not adhere, incubate cells up to 4 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Increase laminin concentration during dish coating to enhance adherence of tumorspheres.
Top up media with an appropriate volume after ensuring tumorspheres are visibly adherent.
At 70%-80% confluency, remove NCC media from the culture dish.
Add TrypLE to the culture dish in a volume that is 5% of the total media volume.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Transfer dissociated cells to a sterile tube.
Rinse the culture dish with 5-10 mL of PBS and add it to the same tube containing the cells.
Follow appropriate instructions for replating on coated or low-binding dishes, or for use in assays.
Dissociate tumorspheres to prepare a single cell solution of GSCs.
Resuspend GSCs in 1–2 mL of PBS.
Count cells using Trypan Blue as described above.
Adjust the number of cells for injection, ranging from 50,000 to 1,000,000 cells per mouse.
Resuspend the adjusted cell count in a volume of PBS between 5 and 10 μL.
Store tubes on ice before injection.
Perform all in vivo procedures according to Animal Research Ethics Board approved protocols.
Ensure all equipment is sterilized before placing it inside the BSL2 hood for injections.
Set up the anesthetic machine as required.
Place one mouse at a time in the induction chamber until unresponsive.
Determine unresponsiveness by lightly pinching the toes with tweezers.
Anesthetize mice using isoflurane, inducing at 5% and maintaining at 2.5% for surgery.
Weigh and record each mouse prior to placing it on the injection platform.
Cut away hair in a 1 cm x 1 cm area above the right side of the frontal lobe.
Expose the skin region for incision.
Use three sterile cotton swabs to scrub the incision site with 10% iodine solution.
Follow up by scrubbing the site with 70% isopropanol.
Finally, scrub the site with 7.5% iodine solution.
Using surgical scissors, cut a 0.5–1 cm opening along the middle of the disinfected area.
Cut a 1 cm opening into the disinfected area using scissors.

Use a Dremel drill with a fine tip for etching, avoiding visible veins and arteries, to reach the brain by applying pressure until it is reached, stopping at no more than 2–3 mm anterior to coronal suture and 3 mm lateral to midline.
Angle the needle 30 degrees anterior to avoid hitting the ventricle.
Draw up and expel 70% ethanol into a Hamilton syringe to clean the syringe.
Rinse the syringe with PBS to ensure any remaining ethanol does not kill cells.
Determine the appropriate amount of cell suspension based on previous calculations.
Prepare an additional 10% of cell suspension to account for pipetting error.
Insert the needle tip no more than 2 mm into the brain through the drill hole.
Slowly inject the cells using a Hamilton syringe at about 0.5 μL/s.
Hold the syringe steady for 2–5 seconds when fully expelled to allow cells to dissipate into the tissue.
Withdraw the syringe slowly at 2 mm/min after holding steadily for 2 minutes to avoid backpressure causing cells to escape out of the brain cavity.
Carefully suture the incision with a double knot of dissolvable vicryl stitches.
Apply a small dab of surgical glue to the knot to prevent mice from reopening the site.
Provide mice with 1 mL of saline and painkiller using single use insulin syringes post-injection.
Place mice back in their cage and provide them with a source of heat to aid in recovery.
Monitor mice regularly until they reach endpoint according to experimental and institutional instructions.
Anesthetize mice with intraperitoneal injection of 25 mg/mL Avertin (18 μL/g of mouse weight) when reaching endpoint.
Wait until mice are unresponsive to toe pinching.
Lay the mouse on its back and tape each limb to the surface while it is unresponsive.
Remove the rib cage and cut the diaphragm to expose the heart without rupturing the lungs or any major circulatory components near the heart.
Inject 20 μL of Heparin sodium directly into the left ventricle of the heart to prevent blood clotting.
Administer 10–50 mL of saline using a 22 gauge needle into the left ventricle of the heart to flush blood from the circulatory system.
Inject 10 mL of 10% formalin into the heart using a 22 gauge needle.
Harvest the brain carefully with scissors and forceps, removing skin and skull while minimizing damage to the brain.
Place the harvested brain in a tube containing 5 mL of 10% formalin.
Store the brain-tube at 4°C for at least 48 hours.
After 48 hours, place the brain in a coronal brain slicing matrix.
Slice the brain into 2 mm sections using razor blades.
Place each 2 mm section into a cassette.
Transfer the cassettes containing the sections into 50% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Move the cassettes from 50% ethanol to 70% ethanol.
Store the samples in 70% ethanol for at least 24 hours.
